experiment: Read-only pure-Python re-derivation of the notebook's cell-37 evaluation split (trainList/testList plus an unseeded shuffle=False train_test_split) and of a seeded whole-session replacement. The notebook was not executed: every input was parsed from the committed notebook JSON. Structural correctness was measured on integer inputs N=0..1000; speed was measured on n=100000 with best-of-5 wall-clock runs. The replacement code is paraphrased from cell 37 and uses the metadata columns that cell 27 already writes.
evidence: Notebook parsed as JSON only; no cell executed, no pip install, no Drive mount, no SEED-V access. process_seedv_raw_files_with_mne_from_drive.ipynb sha256=35d98aa40078b0e6a60b65cf79e2f206827468bb95f1196deeff564cda5142fc before and after the experiment; `git status --porcelain` shows changes only under research/.

Cell 37 source, verbatim: `train_samples = math.floor((training_percent*total_array_samples))`; `trainList = list(range(1, train_samples + 1, 1))`; `testList = list(range(train_samples + 1, total_array_samples, 1))`; `splits = windows_dataset.split({"train": trainList, "test": testList})`; then `train_set = windows_dataset` (discards splits['train']); then `train_indices, val_indices = train_test_split(X_train.indices_, test_size=val_percent, shuffle=False)`. `y_test_set = y[train_samples + 1:]` is scored against test_set.

Recorded dataset size: cell 32 output is 48 label vectors of length 12 = 576 trials, class counts Disgust 144 / Fear 96 / Sad 112 / Neutral 144 / Happy 80. training_percent=0.8 (cell 39) gives train_samples=floor(0.8*576)=460, |testList|=115, and sklearn's shuffle=False split gives |val|=ceil(0.2*576)=116 (indices 460..575).

Test is a subset of validation on the committed literals: test = 461..575 (115), val = 460..575 (116); test minus val = empty, val minus test = {460}, overlap 115/115 = 100% of the test set. So cell 39's 'Test acc' is a re-measurement of validation trials, and because cell 38's validation accuracy is displayed while model_option/training_percent are being chosen, selection has seen every test trial.

Session-block leak, provable at the recorded block size: 576 trials / 48 recorded vectors = 12 consecutive trials per block; 460 mod 12 = 4, so the block at indices 456..467 straddles the train/val boundary. No subject-level ordering claim is made: cells 25/29 are %%capture and print no file names, so the mapping of blocks to subjects and the listdir order are not observable in the repository.

The single recorded number is constant-predictor compatible. On the recorded label vector, always-Neutral scores 115/460 = 25.00% (train), 29/116 = 25.00% (val), 28/115 = 24.35% (test), reproducing the recorded 0.25 / 0.25 (cell 38) and 24.35% (cell 39) exactly. The test-slice majority is Disgust at 29/115 = 25.22%, so the pipeline is below the trivial baseline on its own test slice. Exact binomial: 28/115 vs 0.20 gives p=0.2441; vs 29/115 gives p=0.9146; Wilson 95% CI is [17.42%, 32.94%].

Cell 38's committed intrinsic dataframe summary reports rows=100 and train_accuracy and valid_accuracy each with std=0.0, min=max=0.25, num_unique_values=1; the displayed text/html table is truncated to 10 rows but the summary metadata covers all 100 epochs. Recorded losses are negative (train min -753759.28, max -523.59; valid min -955689.18, max -2314.25) while cell 37 uses criterion=torch.nn.NLLLoss and cell 35's summary shows no log-softmax layer; this is an inconsistency in the recorded run, not a diagnosis and not evidence about model quality.

Provenance correction (supersedes the scouts' label-consistency claim): the committed score tables in cell 24 imply 48 sessions with 7-15 score>=4 trials each, 533 total (98/116/91/134/94 by class), while the committed cell 31/32 outputs show 12 trials per file, 576 total (144/96/112/144/80). The recorded epoch inputs therefore cannot be regenerated from the committed annotation/score cells; the constant-Neutral identity is scoped to the recorded cell-32 label vectors only.

Correctness contract over integer inputs N=0..1000: pairwise-disjoint train/val/test, union = {0..N-1}, and no effective group split across partitions (session blocks when N>=36, per-trial fallback below that). The cell-37 parent passes 6/1001 inputs (N=0..5, where test is empty) and fails disjointness 995 times and group integrity 995 times (all N>=6). The seeded session-grouped replacement passes 1001/1001.

At the recorded N=576 with 48 session blocks the replacement yields train=348 (60.42%), val=120 (20.83%), test=108 (18.75%), all three non-empty and pairwise disjoint; the same seed reproduces the partition exactly and seed=7 produces a different partition. This is a synthetic re-derivation from the committed 48x12 layout, not a run of the notebook.

Speed, wall clock on this machine, best of 5 runs at n=100000: parent cell-37 construction 1.923 ms; seeded session-grouped replacement 8.439 ms (about 4.4x slower, both under 10 ms on 100k trial indices). Timings are machine-specific and say nothing about model accuracy.

Retained improvement, one cell-local edit to cell 37: build trial groups from the metadata that cell 27 already writes (subject and session), shuffle the group order with a fixed seed (e.g. random.Random(20240820)), assign whole groups to train/val/test at 60/20/20 targets, and assert that the three index sets are pairwise disjoint and cover 0..N-1 before constructing train_subset/val_subset/test_set. Keep the declared test_set and y_test_set aligned with that test set; do not reassign train_set to the full windows_dataset. The evaluation split, not the loss, baseline, window length, environment or Drive coupling, is the single retained change; those remain separate findings.
